facts.text: Suwannee’s name may come from the Creek word *sawani*, meaning “echo river,” a theory that still appears in modern scholarship.
The Suwannee River, about 246 miles long, winds through Florida’s panhandle before emptying into the Gulf of Mexico near Suwannee.
Local historians in Suwannee County offer walking tours that pair historic landmarks with stories from the region’s past.
Suwannee County’s Historical Commission, located at 208 Ohio Ave., preserves artifacts and documents that trace the area’s early settlement.
The Suwannee River once formed the prehistoric Suwanee Straits, a natural barrier that separated the Florida peninsula from the mainland.
